div.l: Ful many fat ꝑpartriche had he in mewe
And many a breme and many a luce in stewe
Wo were his coke but hit sauce were
Poynant and sharp and redi all his gere
His table dormaunte in his halle all wey
Stode redi reuerd all þe longe day
At cessions was he lorde and syre
Ful oft tymes he was knight of þe shire
An Anlas and a gipsiar al of silk
Hang at his girdell as whight as morn̄ mylke
A shirrefe hath he be and a countoure
Was no where suche a worthi vauasoure
AN haberdassher and a Carpenter
A Wedde a Dyer and a Tapicer
And þei were clothed al in one lyueraye
Of a solempne and a grete fraternite
Full fressh and newe her gere piked was
Her knifes not chaped was with brasse
But all with siluer wrought clene and wele
Her girdeles and her pouches eueri dele
Wel semed eche of hem a faire burges
To sit in þe yelde hall on a dese
Eueriche one for þe wisdom that he can̄
Was worthi to be an Alderman̄
For Catell had þei I nogh and rente
And eke hir wifes wold well assente
And ellez certein thei were to blame
It is ful faire to be cleped madame
And goon to vigiles all be forne
And haue a mantel rialli I borne
A coke þei hadde for þe nones
To boile þe chekenes with þe mari bones
And poudre marchaunte tarte and galingale
Wel couth he knowe a draught of Ale
He couth roste and seth boile and fry
Make morterewes and wel bake a pie
But grete harme was it as þought me
That on his shyn a mormal had be
For blank manger made he with þe best
A shipman was þer wonnyng be west
For ought I wote he was of dertemouthe
He rode vpon̄ a rouncy as he couthe
In a gown̄ of falding to þe kne
A dagger hanging / in a lace hadde he
